title: Long exception message overflows the red `st.exception` box

labels.name: status:confirmed
labels.description: Bug has been confirmed by the Streamlit team

body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

If you have a long exception message, it overflows the red box below:
![CleanShot 2024-11-08 at 14 44 15](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac66ce05-9ae3-4662-85be-1fe30568d234)


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

raise RuntimeError("jsldfklasjlkdfklsdfjklkjlsdfsdfsdfsdfsdfsdfsdfsdfklsdfkljsdklfjskdjlfkjlsdfkl")
```


### Steps To Reproduce

Run the app above. See playground [here](https://streamlit.io/playground?example=blank&code=H4sIAAAAAAAAA22KQQqAMAwE731F6Ukf4gf8QSEtNNlaSeL_tXoV5jAD0_o51KO5ltzRPGZ7IgTNzUrcr8NbL5vq0CWxgaogG0OmGFUWCE_55V0EbCSobEKM-u2CtN6pASklewAAAA).

### Expected Behavior

Text breaks to next line, similar to if you use e.g. `st.warning` with a long string:
![CleanShot 2024-11-08 at 14 45 36](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/84409066-551c-4789-86c1-67cf08a55164)


### Current Behavior

See screenshot above. 

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.40
- Python version:
- Operating System:
- Browser:

_No response_
